newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares give up initial gains to end lower.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares give up initial gains to end lower.

text.p: 1530 GMT - Swiss shares lost steam in the course of the day, giving up most initial gains and slipping below Friday's close towards the session's end.

"It was a little disappointing today", one dealer said, noting that some investors had hoped for a better performance given the U.S. dollar's rise above 1.40 Swiss francs and Friday's record Wall Street close.
"But we are at a very high level and the air ist getting thin", he said, adding a fall below 4,000 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) seemed likely this week.
* SMI slid 10.3 points, or 0.26 percent, to 4,009.6.
* All-share SPI fell 4.40 points to 2,574.76 points.
Major pharmaceuticals Roche and Novartis were in the limelight, with Novartis suffering from sells by British invesors while Roche continued its bull run, a dealer said.

* Roche powered ahead 120 francs, or 1.09 percent, to 11,170 francs, after hitting a life high at 11,195 earlier in the day. Novartis were pressured by some selling in reaction to steep gains the shares of Ciba and Sandoz had posted ahead of the two companies' merger as Novartis in December, dealers said.
Trade on Swiss Options and Futures Exchange (Soffex) was very quiet, with Credit Suisse, UBS and Roche standing out, dealers said.

In UBS, 19,838 calls and 12,145 puts were traded. In all 11,408 Credit Suisse calls and 4,144 puts changed hands. Volume in Roche options was high with call and put volume reaching around 5,000 contracts. The fact that there were slightly more puts than calls was rather unsual for Roche options, a dealer said. Total volume reached 135,975 contracts.
A total of 2,997 SMI options were traded.
